claims.text: A molybdenum interlayer can enable a high-performance bond between W and CuCrZr.
A molybdenum interlayer reduces the thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
A molybdenum interlayer inhibits detrimental interdiffusion between W and CuCrZr under reactor-relevant conditions.
Molybdenum has physical and chemical properties intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
Molybdenum has an intermediate coefficient of thermal expansion relative to W and CuCrZr.
The intermediate thermal-expansion coefficient of molybdenum reduces mechanical stresses at the W–CuCrZr interface.
A molybdenum interlayer acts as a barrier to interdiffusion at the W–CuCrZr interface.
Reduced interfacial stress and interdiffusion prevent early bond degradation under extreme thermal and irradiation loads.
Mo-containing interlayers will improve bond integrity relative to direct W–CuCrZr joints under reactor operational conditions.
Mo-containing interlayers will reduce interfacial diffusion relative to direct W–CuCrZr joints under reactor operational conditions.
Mo-containing interlayers will enhance joint durability relative to direct W–CuCrZr joints under reactor operational conditions.
Direct W–CuCrZr bonds are prone to high interfacial stresses under thermal cycling.
Direct W–CuCrZr bonds are prone to marked interdiffusion.
Direct W–CuCrZr bonds are prone to premature failure under thermal cycling.
At sufficiently high temperature or irradiation exposure, the Mo interlayer might undergo undesirable phase changes or reactions that limit its benefits.
